subject: Region-bound data disposal: hosted API questions
messages:
From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@starlark.com>
To: alex_martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.example.com>
Cc: privacy@starlark.com
Date: 2028-11-20T09:12:00Z
Subject: Region-bound data disposal: hosted API questions

Hi Alex,

We're evaluating Redwood for a customer-facing analytics feature and have a few concrete questions about hosted API behaviour in EU regions. Our security team asked for short answers we can include in our vendor review: 

1) If we select EU as the ingestion/storage region, will raw request payloads (inputs + outputs) remain within EU-controlled storage for the lifetime they exist?
2) What are the default retention periods for (a) raw request payloads, (b) request/response debugging logs, (c) aggregated telemetry/metrics, and (d) nightly backups?
3) If we request a full erasure for a tenant, what is your timeline to remove data from active systems and from backups?
4) Do you provide a DPA / SCCs and any attestations about data residency?
5) Any caveats where data may transit outside the EU during processing?

We appreciate concise, non-legal answers for now — we'll escalate to formal paperwork once we have the high-level behaviour confirmed.

Thanks,
Ellen
Ellen Park
Security & Privacy Lead, Starlark Analytics
privacy@starlark.com

--
Attachment: security-questionnaire-template.xlsx (referenced, not attached here)

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.example.com>

Cc: grace_oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.example.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.example.com>
Date: 2028-11-20T13:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Region-bound data disposal: hosted API questions

Hi Ellen — thanks for the clear list. High-level answers below; looping in Grace (Product) and Rishi (Security) to confirm specifics and attach the DPA. I also attached a short whitepaper and a regional flow diagram for quick reference.

Quick answers:
- Region residency: Yes — when you choose the EU data plane for your account, persistent storage of request payloads and customer-controlled artifacts is limited to EU regions (we persist in the selected region cluster).
- Default retention: raw request payloads (default) = 30 days; debug logs (request id, metadata, non-user content debug traces) = 7 days; aggregated metrics = 24 months; nightly backups = retained 90 days in encrypted form.
- Erasure timeline: active data removed within 72 hours of an approved erasure request; residual copies in backups are scheduled for cryptographic destruction/rotation within 90 days (we provide confirmation when process completes).
- DPA/SCCs: Yes — we have a DPA with EU SCCs available. Grace will attach the signed DPA link.
- Transit caveats: Model execution may call managed inference caches and runtime nodes within the selected EU region; we do not route EU-stored payloads to non-EU regions for hosting by default. Short-lived inter-service calls (control-plane telemetry) may reach US-based control plane for telemetry/ops unless you opt for Private deployment.

Next steps: Grace/Rishi — can you confirm and expand on backup deletion semantics and whether debug logs ever include user PII in the worst-case? Ellen — if these answers look good I'd be happy to create a short vendor addendum that captures the retention windows for your procurement team.

Best,
Alex
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.example.com

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.example.com>
To: alex.martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.example.com>, Ellen Park <ellen.park@starlark.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.example.com>
Date: 2028-11-21T08:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Region-bound data disposal: hosted API questions

Thanks Alex — confirming and clarifying from product side. A couple of implementation details: 

- EU residency: Customer account metadata pins storage to an EU region (currently eu-west-1 or eu-central-1 clusters). All persistent object stores (request archives, customer configs, model pin records) are created in those regions.
- Raw payload retention: Default "request archive" TTL is 30 days. This archive stores full input and output for the purposes of debugging, billing disputes, and quality monitoring. You may request a stricter TTL at provisioning time or ask for request-archive disabled for your account (some features like fine-grained eval comparisons require archive to be enabled).
- Debug logs: Our application logs capture request_ids, latencies, and anonymized stack traces. We have a separate debug-log pipeline that scrubs user content by default; raw user content is not present in debug logs under normal operation. Debug logs retention is 7 days by default; we can extend/shorten this for enterprise customers.
- Nightly backups: Backups are encrypted, geo-redundant within the EU, and retained for 90 days. We rely on periodic key rotation and backup lifecycle policies; final deletion from backup media is bound by the backup system retention window (90 days).
- Erasure process: We run a three-phase erasure for tenant requests: (1) disable account and stop new writes, (2) delete from active/nearline stores within 72 hours, (3) mark backups for deletion and perform cryptographic key rewrap/rotation and eventual removal within 90 days. We provide a certificate of deletion once complete.

Ellen — happy to include these as the canonical answers for procurement. If Starlark requires shorter backup windows or immediate cryptographic erasure guarantees, that's typically handled as an addendum to the Dedicated/Private offering.

Regards,
Grace O'Connor
Product Manager, Redwood Inference

--
Internal note: feature flag ENABLE_REQUEST_ARCHIVE must be set on provisioning to enable 30d archive; otherwise archive disabled and retention for raw payloads = 0d.

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.example.com>
To: grace.oconnor <grace.oconnor@redwood.example.com>, alex.martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.example.com>, Ellen Park <ellen.park@starlark.com>
Date: 2028-11-21T10:15:00Z
Subject: Re: Region-bound data disposal: hosted API questions

Adding a security confirmation: 

- Proofs & paperwork: We maintain a DPA (with SCCs) and SOC2 Type II report; the DPA link is: https://redwood.example.com/dpa/eu/v2. For customers requiring additional attestations we can share an NDA'd SOC artifact.
- PII in debug logs: By design debug logs are scrubbed; however, if a customer enables verbose debugging we may temporarily retain snippets for triage — such access is gated, audited, and time-limited. We recommend Starlark disable verbose debug for regulated workloads.
- Backups & cryptographic erasure: Our backup storage supports cryptographic key destruction; when a deletion is requested we schedule a key rotation that renders existing backup blobs unreadable before physical deletion. The timeline for that process is within 90 days.

I'll approve these answers for public-facing vendor responses.

- Rishi
Director, Security Engineering, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Region-bound data disposal: hosted API questions

Ellen — consolidating the confirmed answers for your security review. Below is a short, procurement-ready summary and a suggested next step.

Summary (procurement-ready):
- Data residency: When an account is configured for the EU data plane, persistent customer data (request archives, stored configs) are created and kept in EU regions only (eu-west-1 or eu-central-1).
- Retention windows (defaults): raw request archive = 30 days; debug logs (scrubbed) = 7 days; aggregated telemetry/metrics = 24 months; nightly encrypted backups = 90 days.
- Erasure SLA: Active data removed within 72 hours of an approved erasure request; backup/key-revocation-based destruction completed within 90 days. We will issue a deletion confirmation at completion.
- Transit & processing: We do not route EU-stored payloads to non-EU compute regions by default. The control plane may make short telemetry/control calls outside the EU; for strict data locality customers we recommend Redwood Private or Dedicated.
- Paperwork: DPA and SCCs available at https://redwood.example.com/dpa/eu/v2; SOC2 reports available under NDA.

Next step: If this aligns with Starlark's controls, I can generate a two-page vendor response document that maps your security questionnaire fields to our answers and attach the DPA. If you need shorter backup windows or an explicit cryptographic erasure clause, we'll route that to Legal and can propose language tied to Dedicated/Private offerings.

Would you like the vendor response doc now?

Thanks again — happy to schedule a 20-minute call to walk procurement/security through any item.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
